subject: Follow-up: Hosted vs Dedicated - latency/throughput requirements
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>
To: Sam Patel <sam@finpay.com>
Cc: Neha Kapoor <neha@redwood.ai>, Dylan Brooks <dylan@redwood.ai>
Date: Sun, 9 May 2027 10:12:00 -0700
Subject: Follow-up: Hosted vs Dedicated - latency/throughput requirements

Hi Sam —

Thanks again for the call this morning. Quick recap and next steps so we're aligned: 

Call highlights:
- FinPay is evaluating LLM-powered transaction monitoring and customer support features.
- Primary constraints: p95 inference latency target around 50ms for single-turn requests and sustained throughput of ~400-600 req/s during peak windows.
- Sensitive data: PCI-adjacent PII but you're okay with hosted API provided we can meet isolation/retention requirements; you may later consider a Private VPC for audit controls.

My read: given the low p95 latency target + high sustained throughput, Dedicated capacity looks like the most likely fit for initial production (predictable GPU pools and pinned model versions). Hosted API might work for early testing but could struggle to guarantee the 50ms p95 at 500 req/s without reserved capacity.

Next steps I promised:
1) Share a short capacity proposal (attached) with a recommended Dedicated configuration and ballpark committed cost.
2) Run a quick latency/throughput matrix with our runtime team to validate the 50ms p95 at 500 req/s for the model family you indicated.
3) Draft an initial statement of work for pilot + SLA options.

I've looped in Neha (solutions/infra) and Dylan (acct lead) to validate the sizing and timeline.

Would you prefer we proceed with a short Dedicated pilot proposal, or do you want an interim hosted POC to move faster while we prep Dedicated numbers?

Thanks,
Marissa Cole
Senior Account Executive
Redwood Inference

Attachment: 20270509-finpay-map-capacity-proposal.pdf (proposal, 3 pages)

From: Sam Patel <sam@finpay.com>

Date: Sun, 9 May 2027 15:44:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Follow-up: Hosted vs Dedicated - latency/throughput requirements

Marissa,

Thanks for the recap — that aligns with what we discussed. A few clarifications from our side: 
- 50ms p95 is a hard goal for checkout fraud scoring (if p95 slips above ~80ms conversion drops).
- For support chat routing/summary features we can tolerate slightly higher p95 (~150ms), but the fraud path is the priority.
- Peak load estimation: average 200 req/s, spikes to 500-600 req/s for ~10 minutes after promo events.
- We need basic SOC2 evidence and logs retention for 12 months; we'll surface any procurement constraints after the pilot.

I'm fine with Dedicated pilot if you recommend it — speed to market is important but we can handle a short POC timeline. Please include any quick-run test results you can get from your runtime folks.

Best,
Sam
Director of Payments Engineering
FinPay

From: Neha Kapoor <neha@redwood.ai>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>, Dylan Brooks <dylan@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 10 May 2027 13:55:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Fwd: Follow-up: Hosted vs Dedicated - latency/throughput requirements

Marissa / Dylan,

Quick summary from infra/tests after a short bench run (details attached):
- Model: RecommendModel-v2 (8-bit quantized)
- Test: 1k warm requests at target payload size (average token length ~40)
- Observed: p95 = ~62ms on a single A100-80GB pod with optimized kernels and continuous batching tuned for low latency; p95 reduces to ~48ms when colocating two pods behind our routing with per-request KV cache warming.
- At 500 req/s sustained, a two-pod Dedicated pool with autoscale to 3 pods for spike windows met p95 ~50ms in our bench with careful batching (max batch size 12, dynamic batching windows tuned).

Tradeoffs and notes:
- Single pod (A100) is close but marginal for p95 50ms at sustained 500 req/s; we recommend starting with 2 pods reserved + autoscale to 3 for short spikes (10-15min).
- If FinPay wants a safety margin, suggest GPU profile with 2x A100-80GB reserved or 1x H100 + 1x A100 mixed pool (higher cost, lower p95).
- Hosted API: could be used for an initial non-production POC, but cannot provide the same p95 guarantees during noisy neighbors without reserved Dedicated capacity.
- Compliance: we have SOC2 Type II report, 12-month logs retention available as an add-on; Private VPC is an option for stricter network isolation later.

I attached a short capacity sketch and ballpark monthly committed pricing for 2x A100 reserved with autoscale (see 20270509-finpay-map-capacity-proposal.pdf).

Recommendation:
Start with a Dedicated pilot: 2 reserved A100 pods, autoscale to 3 pods, 1 month pilot to validate real traffic patterns, then roll to production commit if p95 targets hold.

-Neha
Principal Solutions Engineer
Redwood Inference

Attachment: finpay-latency-sla-draft.docx (SLA draft, 2 pages)

Hi Sam —

Thanks for the clarifications. Based on a short bench run and Neha's recommendations, here's the concise plan: 

Proposal (Pilot):
- Deployment: Dedicated capacity pilot (2x A100-80GB reserved pods, autoscale to 3 pods for 10-15 minute spikes).
- Rationale: Bench runs indicate ~48-62ms p95 depending on placement; the 2+autoscale config met ~50ms p95 at 500 req/s in our tests and gives headroom for production traffic variability.
- Timeline: 2-week pilot to validate on FinPay traffic patterns (we'll work with your infra to mirror payloads).
- Compliance: We'll include SOC2 artifacts and 12-month logs retention in the SOW; Private VPC remains an option if procurement requires tighter network isolation.
- Next steps: If you agree, I'll send a one-page SOW + pilot PO template and propose kickoff for next week.

Would you like me to proceed with the pilot SOW and PO? If yes, please indicate any procurement constraints (PO cadence, vendor terms).

Best regards,
Marissa Cole
Senior Account Executive
Redwood Inference
